about.disclaimer_body: OSRS Events is a fan-made project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Jagex Ltd. Old School RuneScape is a trademark of Jagex Ltd.
about.feature_boards_desc: Run a Snakes & Ladders board with an OSRS task on every tile, or a skill race scored straight off the hiscores.
about.feature_dark_desc: Easy on the eyes whether you grind at noon or 2 AM. Dark mode is always available.
about.feature_dice_desc: On a board, roll a d6 each day and advance. Roll limits keep it competitive without turning it into a grind.
about.feature_discord_desc: Log in with Discord, or with an email address if you prefer. Either way your progress is saved automatically.
about.feature_free_desc: No premium tiers, no paywalls. Everything is free. If you enjoy it, consider a donation!
about.feature_tasks_desc: Every board tile has an OSRS task. Complete it in-game and mark it done to unlock your next roll.
about.free_body: This project is run by a player, for players. Hosting and maintenance cost real money, so if you find value in the platform, a small donation helps keep the lights on.
about.privacy_body: We collect the minimum needed to run the platform — your Discord username, ID and avatar if you log in that way, or your email address if you sign up directly, plus the OSRS account name used to score you in events. We do not track you, show you ads, or sell your data to anyone. Full details are in our Privacy Policy.
about.subtitle: An OSRS-themed events platform for clans, made with love for the community.
about.support_body: Have a question, found a bug, or want to suggest a feature? Send me an email and I'll get back to you as soon as I can.

admin.site_announcement_public_desc: Only does anything while the pre-launch lock is on. Off, the announcement is for people already using the site. On, it also shows on the lock screen — for a launch date, a call for beta testers, or a Discord link.
admin.site_defaults_desc: Pre-filled when someone creates an event. They can still change them per event.
admin.site_discord_webhooks_desc: Lets a host paste a Discord webhook into their event, so pausing, resuming or cancelling it posts one line in their clan's channel. Off until it has been tried against a real server — while it is off the field is hidden and nothing is ever sent.
admin.site_event_duration_desc: How long a new event is pre-filled to run for. Days, or a short form like 2w or 1m.
admin.site_kofi_url_desc: Every "Support" button on the site opens this directly. Use the full profile URL — the bare domain just lands people on Ko-fi's homepage.
admin.site_lock_desc: Shuts the app to new visitors without the shared password. Anyone already signed in — any account, not only admins — keeps full use of the site; this only stops strangers from wandering in or signing up.
admin.site_lock_note: The public pages, the lock screen and the login pages stay reachable — the app itself redirects a stranger until they enter the password, sign in with an existing account, or sign in as an admin. New accounts are closed while it is on. This is not maintenance mode; the site keeps running normally behind it.

admin.site_full_lockdown_note: Only an admin session gets through. The public pages are refused too — this is meant to take the whole app away, not just keep it quiet. Turn the pre-launch lock on instead if the goal is only to keep new visitors and new accounts out while existing players keep going.

diagnostics.description: Everything that can fail without saying so, asked out loud.
diagnostics.group_mail_desc: The password-reset link is the only thing that sends mail, so this is the easiest thing in the app to leave broken.
diagnostics.group_push_desc: Keys, encryption, and the devices registered to receive.
diagnostics.group_rendering_desc: Server-side rendering fails to client rendering silently — the browser looks perfect, the served HTML is empty.
diagnostics.group_schedule_desc: Without the cron entry, standings never move and five of the nine notification categories never fire.
diagnostics.group_wom_desc: Where every race's numbers come from. When it stops answering, a leaderboard just stops moving.
diagnostics.mail_driver_fix: Password reset is dead in this state, with nothing in the logs saying so. Set MAIL_MAILER to smtp.
diagnostics.mail_driver_log: log — writes to storage/logs and reports success. Nothing is delivered.
diagnostics.mail_from_default: :address — the placeholder, which is neither verified nor yours.
diagnostics.mail_from_fix: An unverified From gets rejected or filed as spam. Set MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS to an address at a domain you verified.
diagnostics.mail_queue_detail: Event status mail is queued on the :driver driver. With no worker consuming it, those jobs sit unsent forever.
diagnostics.push_encryption_bad: OpenSSL cannot generate a P-256 key, so every send fails.
diagnostics.push_encryption_fix: Check that this PHP has the openssl extension and can generate EC keys.
diagnostics.push_encryption_fix_windows: OPENSSL_CONF is not set, which is the usual cause on Windows. A queue worker needs it in its own environment, not just your shell.
diagnostics.push_encryption_ok: OpenSSL can generate the per-message key
diagnostics.push_key_fix: The key was pasted wrong. Copy it again from webpush:vapid, whole.
diagnostics.push_keys_fix: Run php artisan webpush:vapid and add the three VAPID_ variables to this environment.
diagnostics.push_keys_missing: Not configured — nothing can be sent to anyone.
diagnostics.push_pair_bad: MISMATCH — these two halves belong to different keys.
diagnostics.push_pair_fix: Every send will be accepted and delivered to nobody. Replace both halves with one generated pair.
diagnostics.push_pair_ok: The private key derives this public key
diagnostics.push_stale_detail: :count device(s) subscribed against a different VAPID key.
diagnostics.push_stale_fix: Those will never receive anything again — the push service still accepts sends to them. They have to turn notifications on again in the app.
diagnostics.push_subject_bad: Must be a mailto: or https: URL.
diagnostics.push_subject_fix: Apple rejects anything else outright, and says nothing about which field was wrong.
diagnostics.push_subject_placeholder: :subject — still the example address from the generator.
diagnostics.push_subject_placeholder_fix: Push services use this to reach you about a misbehaving app. An address nobody reads turns a warning into a block. Set VAPID_SUBJECT to a real contact.
diagnostics.render_bundle_fix: The SSR process has nothing to load. Run pnpm build:ssr as part of the deploy.
diagnostics.render_hot_absent: Absent, as it should be outside a dev server
diagnostics.render_hot_fix: A killed dev server leaves it behind and every page then ships an empty div. Delete public/hot.
diagnostics.render_hot_present: public/hot exists, which silently switches SSR off.
diagnostics.render_process_detail: Loads the bundle once at startup and never re-reads it, so a deploy that rebuilds without restarting keeps serving the previous build. Not checkable from here — restart it on every deploy.
diagnostics.schedule_fix: The scheduler is probably not running. Add the cron entry that runs php artisan schedule:run every minute.
diagnostics.schedule_never: Has never completed on this environment.
diagnostics.sweep_desc: Runs the notification sweep as a dry run and shows what it found. Nothing is sent — the real run belongs to the scheduler, and a button that buzzes thirty phones is not a diagnostic.
diagnostics.test_mail_body: This is a test message from :app. If you are reading it, mail transport works.
diagnostics.test_mail_desc: Sends a plain message to your own address. It proves transport only — with the log driver it will report success and deliver nothing.
diagnostics.test_mail_no_address: Your account has no email address. A Discord login never asks for one — add one under account settings.
diagnostics.test_mail_sent: Sent to :address. Check the inbox, and the spam folder.
diagnostics.test_push_desc: Sends one real encrypted push to your own devices. It is the only way to prove the last hop — the push service to the handset — which nothing else can check.
diagnostics.test_push_failed: The push service refused it. Check the key pair above.
diagnostics.test_push_no_devices: No devices registered. Turn notifications on for this browser in your notification settings first.
diagnostics.test_push_sent: Sent to :count device(s). If nothing arrives, the failure is past this server.
diagnostics.test_push_unconfigured: No VAPID keys configured, so nothing could be sent.

diagnostics.wom_agent_fix: Set WOM_USER_AGENT to something with an email or URL in it, so they can ask you to stop before blocking you.

diagnostics.wom_check_unreachable: No answer from Wise Old Man. Standings will not update until it comes back.

landing.clan_events.setup_body: Start smaller than you think you should. A 5×5 board over a weekend tells you how your clan actually engages, and costs an afternoon to build. Set a daily roll limit so the event paces itself rather than being finished by Sunday. Write your tasks to be checkable from a screenshot — 'get a Dragon Warhammer' settles cleanly, 'do some slayer' does not. Then post the board link in your Discord and pin it, because the single most common reason a clan event dies is that half the roster never found the link.

landing.clan_events.why_body: A clan is at its healthiest when members log in with a reason to. Events give the roster a shared goal, pull semi-inactive members back, and give newer players a way to contribute that does not depend on gear or kill count. The idea was never the hard part — the tracking was. Most clans end up with a spreadsheet nobody updates and a Discord thread of screenshots nobody reads.

landing.drop_race.why_body: A drop race is really a killcount race — it measures how many times you killed the chosen boss during the event, not what actually dropped. That keeps it fair regardless of RNG: a player who kills the boss a hundred times without a single unique still outranks someone who got lucky on kill three but stopped there.
landing.event_ideas.idea1_desc: Every tile is an OSRS task and players roll a daily d6 to advance. Ladders jump you forward, snakes drop you back. Because a dice roll sits between a player and their next task, hours played matter less than in any other format here — a casual member can genuinely beat a maxed main, which keeps the event competitive to the final day.
landing.event_ideas.idea2_desc: A grid of drop or achievement tiles; teams race to complete rows, columns or the full board. Far and away the most popular OSRS event format, and the most demanding. It rewards raw hours, so a few grinders usually decide it early unless you weight the tiles carefully.
landing.event_ideas.idea3_desc: Pick a boss, and everyone races on kill count gained from the moment they join — synced automatically, not a manual log of what actually dropped, so a string of bad luck doesn't cost a player the event the way it would if uniques were what scored.
landing.event_ideas.idea4_desc: Everyone starts from their current XP in a chosen skill and races for the biggest gain. Fair by construction, because it measures change rather than total: a level 60 and a level 99 compete on equal terms.
landing.event_ideas.idea5_desc: Post a fixed set of encounters and let members submit times. It runs indefinitely with no end date, which makes it the lowest-maintenance option on this list — good as a permanent background event between bigger ones.
landing.event_ideas.idea6_desc: Points for diary tiers or quests completed inside the event window. One of the few formats where newer accounts have the advantage, since veterans have already finished everything. Excellent for onboarding a wave of new members.
landing.event_ideas.idea7_desc: Each team hides ships on a grid and fires by completing tasks. Very social and very chat-heavy, but it needs an organiser watching it daily — the format lives or dies on somebody refereeing it.
landing.event_ideas.idea8_desc: Track collection log slots filled across the whole clan against one shared target. Cooperative rather than competitive, which suits clans where a leaderboard would put people off rather than draw them in.

landing.event_ideas.intro: The best clan event is the one your members finish. A format that carries a 200-member PvM clan will die quietly in a 15-person social clan, and the reverse is just as true. Below is what each format actually rewards, so you can choose on purpose instead of copying whatever the last clan did.

landing.event_ideas.pick_body: Two questions settle it. First: how much time does your median member have — not your most active one? Formats that reward raw hours reward the top ten percent of your roster and quietly tell everybody else not to bother. Second: who is going to run it? Every format above needs somebody approving completions and answering questions daily. If nobody has volunteered for that yet, run a shorter event than the one you want.

landing.snakes.host_step1_desc: Pick 5×5, 7×7 or 9×9, name the event, and set the start and end dates — the size decides how long the event runs, not how big your clan is.
landing.snakes.host_step2_desc: Open a tile and search the OSRS Wiki right there — the icon and title fill themselves in, so "assign a task" is one search box, not a form per tile.
landing.snakes.host_step3_desc: Turn any tile into a snake or a ladder and pick where it sends a player. A board with no surprises is just a checklist with extra steps.
landing.snakes.host_step4_desc: Open it to anyone, lock it to your Discord server, or hand out invite links you can revoke later — decided once, changeable any time from Manage.
landing.snakes.host_step5_desc: Share the board link or drop it in your Discord. Anyone who rolls the dice is counted as joined — there's no separate "sign up" step for them.

landing.snakes.lead: A free Snakes & Ladders board built for Old School RuneScape clans. Every tile is an OSRS task — complete it to keep climbing, or hit a snake and slide back down.
landing.snakes.player_step1_desc: Open the board and roll — playing IS joining. There's no separate sign-up; your first roll creates your own piece on the board.
landing.snakes.player_step2_desc: Land somewhere new, and that tile becomes your current task — shown with its icon, its title and a "You are here" label so it's never ambiguous which one counts.
landing.snakes.player_step3_desc: Do it in-game, then mark the tile complete. Land on a ladder and you jump ahead; land on a snake and you slide back — either way, the next roll is tomorrow's.
landing.snakes.player_step4_desc: One roll a day by default (a host can raise the limit or remove it), so the board is a marathon everyone can keep up with, not a race the first person to log off wins.
landing.snakes.player_subtitle: What actually happens once you open a board someone invited you to.
landing.snakes.meta_desc: Build a free Old School RuneScape Snakes & Ladders board for your clan. Assign OSRS tasks to every tile, roll a daily d6 and track everyone's progress.
landing.snakes.meta_title: OSRS Snakes & Ladders — Free Board Generator
landing.snakes.modes_body: Solo boards give every player their own position and their own daily roll. Team boards give each team one shared position, so the team decides together which task to take on next. Teams can be tied to your Discord server so members are grouped automatically instead of by hand.
landing.snakes.screenshot_editor_alt: The tile editor, showing the OSRS Wiki search open mid-search on a boss name, used to attach an icon and task to a board tile.
landing.snakes.screenshot_board_alt: A live board mid-event, showing the snake and ladder connectors, the current player's "You are here" tile, the dice roller and the current task card.
landing.snakes.size_5_desc: A weekend event. A good first run, and enough for a smaller clan.
landing.snakes.size_7_desc: The usual pick. Comfortably fills one to two weeks of play.
landing.snakes.size_9_desc: A month-long clan event, with room for genuine long-grind tasks.
landing.snakes.sizes_subtitle: Pick the size from how long you want the event to run, not from how big your clan is.
landing.snakes.title: OSRS Snakes & Ladders
landing.snakes.why_body: Bingo rewards whoever grinds the most hours, so the clan's biggest account usually settles it in the first weekend and everyone else stops paying attention. Snakes & Ladders puts a dice roll between a player and their next task. That single change means a casual member can climb past a maxed main, and the event stays live to the final day instead of being decided early.

profile.delete_account_desc: This removes your account and everything personal to it — your settings, your notification devices, your Discord server list and your access to events. It cannot be undone.
profile.delete_confirm_help: Your RuneScape name. Typed out rather than a checkbox, because this deletes other people's progress as well as yours.
profile.delete_confirmation_mismatch: That is not your RuneScape name. Nothing has been deleted.
profile.delete_end_it: End it — frozen in place, nothing lost
profile.delete_end_it_hint: Nothing about the event, its board, or anyone's progress changes — every tile, standing and position stays exactly as it is. It just stops accepting new rolls or completions, and you're removed as its owner. There's no "deleted player" placeholder left behind for you here — you simply won't be listed as an editor any more, the same as if you'd never been added.

profile.delete_everything_confirm: Delete ":name" and every event and team you own — hard, with everyone's progress? This skips the per-item choices above and answers all of them the same way: gone.
profile.delete_everything_desc: Skips the choices above. Every event and team you own is hard-deleted along with everyone's progress on them, the same as choosing "Delete it" for each one — nothing is handed over, nothing is just ended.
profile.delete_hard: Delete it — event and progress, gone for good
profile.delete_hard_hint: Not just hidden: every player's board position, completed tile, standing and bingo square on this event is deleted outright. The event's own settings stay behind as an empty shell an admin can restore, but what happened on it cannot come back.
profile.delete_history_kept: Events that have already finished stay as they are, including :count you took part in. Your name is removed from them — they will show a deleted player.
profile.delete_modal_desc: This is the one action on this page that cannot be undone.
profile.delete_needs_decisions: Something you run changed while this page was open. Reload it, then try again.
profile.delete_no_candidates: Nobody else is in this one, so it's between ending it and deleting it.
profile.delete_settle_confirm: Settle this one now? It happens immediately — your account is not deleted, only this one decision is acted on.
profile.delete_team_end_it: End it — delete the team and its progress
profile.delete_team_end_it_hint: Not just unassigned: every board and bingo card position this team holds is deleted with it — dice position, completed tiles, claimed squares, all of it. This cannot be undone.
